rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should test a baseline multimodal configuration to establish performance benchmarks. This experiment tests the effectiveness of combining RNA (pca_n2000) and image (resnet50) modalities with simple concatenation fusion. It clarifies whether multimodal approaches outperform single-modality baselines, which is critical for guiding subsequent experiments.

The existing evidence shows that config_016 (multimodal, concat fusion) achieves 52.66% accuracy. This experiment tests changing fusion from concat to weighted, isolating its impact on performance. This clarifies whether weighted fusion improves accuracy, a critical design choice, while keeping other factors (model setting, encoders, aggregation) constant. It balances exploitation (building on multimodal approach) and exploration (testing fusion variants).

The existing evidence shows that multimodal singleprofile models with pca_n2000 and resnet50 achieve ~0.526 accuracy. The uncertainty lies in whether multiprofile settings or aggregation methods improve performance. This experiment tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation (a key design choice) while keeping fusion as concat, isolating the effect of profile setting and aggregation. It balances exploration of multiprofile (which may capture more data patterns) and exploitation of proven components (resnet50, concat fusion).

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, and concat fusion (config_018) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.6186). This experiment tests replacing the image encoder (resnet50 → imagenet_vit_l) while keeping aggregation and fusion consistent, isolating the impact of the image encoder. This is the best use of the next experiment as it directly evaluates a key design choice (image encoder) that could improve performance without changing multiple variables.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings, pca_n2000 RNA encoder, and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (e.g., config_024) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.6287). This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from concat to weighted (while keeping other parameters identical) improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. This is a low-risk, high-impact comparison that could either confirm or refine the effectiveness of the current top-performing configuration.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with pca_n2000 and imagenet_vit_l encoders achieve high accuracy (0.6352). This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool aggregation with transformer aggregation (while keeping weighted fusion) improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It builds on the current best configuration by exploring a critical design choice with minimal parameter changes.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with imagenet_vit_l and avgpool perform best (config_025: 0.6352). This experiment tests replacing pca_n2000 RNA encoder with scvi_n200 while keeping image encoder, aggregation, and fusion unchanged. It isolates the impact of RNA encoder choice, a critical design decision, and could either confirm or improve upon the current best performance.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings, scvi_n200 RNA encoder, and imagenet_vit_l image encoder achieve high accuracy (config_037: 0.706). This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool aggregation with transformer aggregation (while retaining weighted fusion) could further improve performance. It isolates the effect of aggregation method on a high-performing baseline, balancing exploitation of current strengths with exploration of architectural variations.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_039) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.724989). This experiment tests whether using scgpt as the RNA encoder in the same setup (config_051) could further improve performance, isolating the effect of the RNA encoder choice. It is the best use of the final experiment to compare competing RNA representations in the most promising architectural configuration.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal, multiprofile models with scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l (e.g., config_039) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests the effect of using concat fusion instead of weighted fusion with transformer aggregation, isolating the impact of fusion strategy. It clarifies whether the previously observed high performance (config_039) depends on weighted fusion or if concat fusion could also yield strong results, leveraging the strong foundation of scvi_n200 and transformer aggregation.
